rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296393400000000}Enemies? What do you mean? There shouldn't be anyone for us to fight.

{C:81930600}{C:819582963A3400000000}Calm down! If you're a man, stop panicking!

{C:81930100}{C:819582963B3400000000}Dad?

{C:81930600}{C:819582963C3400000000}Good, you can hear me. We don't have a ship, so there's no way for us to get to you.

{C:819582963D3400000000}I'll give you instructions from the ground. Just hold out somehow.

{C:81930300}{C:819582963E3400000000}No way! That's impossible, Dad!

{C:81930600}{C:819582963F3400000000}It's all right. You two can do this. I'll give you a quick explanation of combat.

{C:81958296403400000000}If you follow my instructions in battle, you should at least be able to prevent damage to the town. Do your best.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296413400000000}Got it. I'll try!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296423400000000}First, calm down and look at the top of the monitor.

{C:81958296433400000000}You should see values marked HP and EN there. Do you see them?

{C:81930100}{C:81958296443400000000}The top of the screen? ...Oh, this. I found it, Dad.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296453400000000}All right. First, HP. The value marked {C:819782830600}HP{C:819782830000} shows Norstan's durability.

{C:81958296463400000000}In other words, when Norstan's HP reaches 0, you lose--

{C:81958296473400000000}And if you reduce the enemy's HP to 0, you win. Do you understand?

{C:81930100}{C:81958296483400000000}Yeah. So before Norstan runs out of HP...

{C:81958296493400000000}...we just need to bring their ship's HP down to 0, right?

{C:81930600}{C:819582964A3400000000}Exactly.

{C:819582964B3400000000}Next is the value marked {C:819782830600}EN{C:819782830000}. That shows Norstan's energy.

{C:819582964C3400000000}Almost every action the ship takes, such as deploying units, consumes EN.

{C:819582964D3400000000}If you run short of EN when it matters most, it could even get you killed. Never waste it.

{C:819582964E3400000000}Now I'll explain attacking.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582964F3400000000}In combat, each side has its own turns. A turn is divided into a defense phase and an attack phase.

{C:81958296503400000000}You attack while the enemy defends, then the enemy attacks while you defend. Battle repeats that cycle.

{C:81958296513400000000}Since our side has the initiative, this battle begins with the attack phase of your turn.

{C:81958296523400000000}Now I'll explain the battlefield.

{C:81958296533400000000}There are {C:819782830600}lanes{C:819782830000} connecting the two sides. They show where units can deploy.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native body, source cues, cursor, portrait and continuation margin checked at original Kanji name. Forced exact-request tutorial preview; original condition unverified.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296543400000000}There are six of these lanes. Deployed units occupy them according to their width.

{C:81958296553400000000}The basic unit width for FTs and GTs is 2.

{C:81958296563400000000}That means a maximum of three machines can stand side by side.



{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296583400000000}So there's a front and a rear. What's the difference?


{C:81930600}{C:81958296593400000000}In Forward, a unit takes damage more easily, but it also has an easier time attacking.

{C:819582965A3400000000}In Back, it's the reverse. A unit takes damage less easily, but it has a harder time attacking.

{C:819582965B3400000000}Decide which position is best based on the enemy's situation and the units you can deploy.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582965F3400000000}When a unit runs out of HP, it's damaged. It can't launch from the ship until it receives at least basic repairs.

{C:81958296603400000000}Units are repaired every turn, though.

{C:81958296613400000000}If several units are broken, you can't choose which unit will be repaired that turn.

{C:81958296623400000000}To fight reliably, try to avoid having your units damaged as much as possible.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296633400000000}Got it. I'll do my best.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296643400000000}As for their EN, you can basically think of it the same way as a ship's EN.

{C:81958296653400000000}Next, I'll explain unit attributes.

{C:81958296663400000000}First, units have location attributes: {C:819782830600}Ground{C:819782830000}, {C:819782830600}Anti-Air{C:819782830000} and {C:819782830600}Flying{C:819782830000}.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296673400000000}For example, this {C:819782830400}GT-B{C:819782830000} has the Anti-Air location attribute.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296683400000000}And {C:819782830400}GT-A{C:819782830000} has the Ground location attribute.

{C:81958296693400000000}When units have the same location attribute, there is no attribute-related change.

{C:819582966A3400000000}But when units with different attributes fight, it has a major effect.

{C:81958296C43A00000000}Basically, Ground has an advantage over Anti-Air, Flying over Ground, and Anti-Air over Flying.

{C:819582966C3400000000}Remembering that three-way relationship should help you.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582966D3400000000}Next, I'll explain the other kind of attribute.

{C:819582966E3400000000}Each unit has a distance at which it can attack.

{C:819582966F3400000000}There are {C:819782830600}Long Range{C:819782830000} and {C:819782830600}Short Range{C:819782830000} units, plus {C:819782830600}Piercing units{C:819782830000} that attack at both ranges at once.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296703400000000}In general, {C:819782830600}units that attack at Long Range{C:819782830000}, like GT-B, are best suited to fighting from the rear.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296713400000000}And {C:819782830600}units that attack at Short Range{C:819782830000}, like GT-A, are probably better suited to the front.

{C:81958296723400000000}Short Range, Long Range and Piercing are called {C:819782830600}range attributes{C:819782830000}. Remember those terms.

{C:81958296733400000000}Now, back to how combat proceeds.

{C:81958296743400000000}Once you've deployed a unit, you need to give it orders.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296753400000000}A deployed unit won't act unless you give it orders like these. Don't forget.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296763400000000}Giving units action orders consumes EN for each unit.

{C:81958296773400000000}Just like a ship, a unit can't move if it doesn't have enough EN. Be careful.

{C:81958296783400000000}Once you've finished all your actions and orders, select Turn End. Your units will advance against the enemy.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930C00}{C:819582967A3400000000}So they're taking orders from the ground. They have no combat experience at all... Pathetic.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582967B3400000000}The enemy unit that's appeared seems to be a Ground unit.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582967C3400000000}The enemy unit seems to have chosen defense.

{C:819582967D3400000000}A defending opponent can reduce your Attack Power by using up its Defense Power.

{C:819582967E3400000000}That Defense Power is only spent for the current turn. It recovers completely on the next turn.

{C:819582967F3400000000}But that also means Defense Power never recovers during a turn. Each attack just uses up more of it.

{C:81958296803400000000}If you can use up all its Defense Power and bring it to 0, you'll be able to deal damage.

{C:81958296813400000000}Against a defending opponent, you need enough attacks in one turn to exceed its Defense Power.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296823400000000}Once the enemy finishes choosing its actions, each unit will start carrying out its orders.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296833400000000}Units carry out their actions in order, starting with the fastest.

{C:81958296843400000000}Basically, units advance toward the enemy ship in order to attack it.

{C:81958296853400000000}And when units from opposing sides occupy the same lane, they fight.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296863400000000}As I thought, a defending unit isn't easy to bring down...

{C:81930100}{C:81958296873400000000}Damn it!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296883400000000}...But GT-B is next.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296893400000000}Huh?

{C:81930600}{C:819582968A3400000000}As you probably know, GT-B is a Long Range unit.

{C:819582968B3400000000}Normally, ground units can't pass either friend or foe occupying the same lane.

{C:819582968C3400000000}But GT-B is a Long Range unit, so it can attack one step beyond the normal range...

{C:819582968D3400000000}...which means it can hit the enemy in front of GT-A.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:819582968E3400000000}By using Long Range and Short Range units together like this, you can make successive attacks.

{C:81930100}{C:819582968F3400000000}Oh, I see.

{C:81930600}{C:81958296903400000000}But! There's something you need to watch out for when planning successive attacks.


{C:81958296913400000000}Even if you put a Short Range unit in Forward and a Long Range unit in Back, as we just did...

{C:81958296923400000000}...if the Short Range unit in Forward is slower than the Long Range unit in Back...

{C:81958296933400000000}...the Long Range unit can't advance. Its turn will end before it can reach the enemy.

{C:81958296943400000000}Speed can lead to mistakes in all sorts of other situations too. ...Be careful.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930C00}{C:81958296953400000000}They're doing quite well for their first battle...


{C:81930100}{C:81958296963400000000}Dad, it looks like they're going to attack!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296973400000000}Don't panic! First, take a good look around and understand the situation.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296983400000000}Got it!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296993400000000}Listen. When you go from defense to attack, your ship and units recover.

{C:819582969A3400000000}Specifically, the ship's EN and the units' EN are replenished...


{C:819582969B3400000000}...and units aboard the ship recover HP.

{C:819582969C3400000000}Also, one damaged unit finishes its repairs and can be deployed again.



{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:819582969D3400000000}What?! That unit's back?!

{C:81930600}{C:819582969E3400000000}Don't worry. It's repaired, but its HP shouldn't have recovered yet. If it launches now, it can't match you.

{C:819582969F3400000000}More importantly... it looks like another unit's on its way.

{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296A13400000000}That unit farther back... Didn't it just change lanes?

{C:81930600}{C:81958296A23400000000}Yes, it definitely moved. ...Right. I'd better explain that too.

{C:81958296A33400000000}Units already deployed can spend EN to move to an adjacent lane, or between Forward and Back.

{C:81958296A43400000000}Of course, units with their actions already decided can't move. Neither can units boxed in by other units.



{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296A93400000000}All right, you get out there too!

{C:81930100}{C:81958296AA3400000000}...Huh? Oh, right!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296AB3400000000}Their units have the Ground attribute, so the Flying unit {C:819782830400}Impulse 7{C:819782830000} should have the advantage.

{C:81930100}{C:81958296AC3400000000}All right! You can count on me!


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930100}{C:81958296AD3400000000}Whoa!

{C:81958296AE3400000000}Dad! Even with an advantage, I can't take on two units at once!

{C:81930600}{C:81958296B03400000000}Don't panic. Listen carefully!

{C:81958296B13400000000}Against multiple units, Attack Power, Defense Power and damage are split according to the width in contact.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296B23400000000}In this formation, GT-A takes 2/3 of the damage it would take fighting alone.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296B33400000000}The upper GT-A also takes 2/3 of the damage it would take on its own.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296B43400000000}Impulse 7 takes 1/3 of the damage from each opponent, for a total of 2/3.


{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296B53400000000}That example was about the damage our side takes.

{C:81958296B63400000000}Now consider our attacks. Each enemy faces a GT-A, and on top of that...

{C:81958296B73400000000}...each has to take half of Impulse 7's attack as well.

{C:81958296B83400000000}Do you understand? Then get out there!





{x00}
rows.notes: Complete native English row checked on fresh standard72 with original Kanji name. Body, exact cues/cursor and continuation margin pass. Earlier widest-name scope remains in versioned70 evidence; no unseen-page approval.

rows.en:
{C:81930C00}{C:81958296B93400000000}The orders from the ground are accurate. This might take a little longer...



{x00}

rows.en:
{C:81930600}{C:81958296BE3400000000}And you can't use Return during the defense phase.

{C:81958296BF3400000000}Make sure you remember that.

{C:81958296C03400000000}All right, let's finish this in one push!




{x00}

{C:81930C00}{C:81958296C13400000000}It looks as though every unit has launched from Norstan...


{x00}
